description: Demolition of  existing dwelling and annex building and redevelopment of site to provide 4nos new homes with associated amenity space, landscaping, car and cycle parking
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall begin before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.Reason: This is required by Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

Prior to the commencement of any development above ground level (excluding demolition works), samples of the facing materials to be utilised in the development to which this permission relates, including all external facing materials (including external lighting) and boundary treatments, gates, fences (including details of manufacturing specification) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved samples. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance on completion of the development, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

(a) No above ground works (excluding demolition works) shall commence on site until a detailed schedule and specification including manufacturer's literature or detailed drawings (at a scale of 1:5; 1:10, 1:25), in respect of the following has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority: Openings (windows, doors) Rainwater hopper and drainpipes Hard landscaping materials; and Brickwork, bond, mortar and pointing (b) The developer shall submit a site plan / elevation and key plans / elevations where applicable associated with each detail identifying the location of each typical detail to comply with the requirements of part (a). (c) The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved drawings. Reason: To ensure that the local planning authority may be satisfied as to the external appearance of the building(s) and to comply with Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to commencement of any development on site, a Construction Management Plan detailing the following shall be submitted to the planning authority for written agreement:(a) Provision for loading/unloading materials;(b) Storage of plant, materials and operatives vehicles;(c) Signing system for works traffic;(d) Measures for the laying of dust, suppression of noise and abatement of other nuisance arising from development works;(e) Means of enclosure of the site;(f) Wheel washing equipment;(g) The parking of vehicles of the site operatives and visitors; and (h) The erection and maintenance of security hoarding.The development shall only be implemented in accordance with the details and measures approved as part of the construction management plan, which shall be maintained throughout the entire construction period.Reason: In order to safeguard the amenities of the surrounding residential occupiers and to safeguard highway safety and the free flow of traffic in accordance with Policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The mains water consumption of the development hereby approved shall be compliant with the Optional Requirement set out in Part G of the Building Regulations of 105 litres or less per head per day. Reason: In order to minimise the use of mains water and to comply with Policy SI 5 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the 4 secure cycle stores (1 store per house) as shown on the approved plans have been fully implemented and made available for use. Once implemented the cycle stores shall thereafter be retained for use at all times.Reason: To ensure the provision of satisfactory cycle storage facilities and in the interests of sustainable travel choice in accordance with Policy T5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DM8 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the 4 refuse stores (1 store per house) as shown on the approved plans have been fully implemented and made available for use. Once implemented the refuse stores shall thereafter be retained for use at all times.The developer and/or their successors in title shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that all refuse and recyclable materials associated with the development are either stored within these facilities or internally within the building(s) on the application site, and that no refuse or recycling material is stored or placed for collection on the public highway except on the day of collection.Reason: To ensure proper waste management in the interests of the character and appearance of the area and the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy SI7 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Adena Fire Safety Services Ltd Fire Statement Issue 1.0 dated 02 July 2025.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021).

If, during the course of development, any contamination is found which has not been previously identified, work shall be suspended and additional measures for its remediation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation of the site shall incorporate the approved additional measures, and a verification report for all the remediation works shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that risks from land contamination are minimised, in accordance with policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no windows shall be inserted nor any other openings formed (other than those expressly authorised by this permission) to the dwellinghouses unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no additions or enlargements to any dwellinghouses on the site (other than those expressly authorised by this permission) shall be erected unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The flat roof areas of the development to which this permission relates shall not be used as roof gardens, balconies, seating areas or other similar amenity areas, and shall not be accessed except for the purpose of maintenance or in the case of emergency.Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to beneficial occupation of the development to which this permission relates, the following windows shall be constructed so that no part of the framework less than 1.7m above finished floor level shall be openable. Any part below that level shall be fitted with and permanently retained in obscure glazing to a minimum of level 3 on the standard scale. Any film used to achieve the requisite obscurity level shall be non-perishable, tamper-proof, and shall be replaced immediately in the event that it ceases to result in obscurity to level 3:House 2 - First floor south-western facing flank windows (as shown on dwgs: UEL03-MAA-03-XX-DG-A-0002 Rev P06 and UEL03-MAA-04-XX-DG-A-2004-P04 ).House 3 - First floor north-eastern facing flank windows (as shown on dwgs: UEL03-MAA-03-XX-DG-A-0002 Rev P06 and UEL03-MAA-04-XX-DG-A-2005-P01).House 4 - First floor south-western facing flank windows (as shown on dwgs: UEL03-MAA-03-XX-DG-A-0002 Rev P06 and UEL03-MAA-04-XX-DG-A-2006-P01).Reason: To preserve privacy of future and neighbouring occupiers and to comply with DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to the commencement of the development (including demolition works) the developer shall submit a full desk-based archaeological study report to the Local Planning Authority for its written approval.In the event that archaeological interest is identified the developer shall adhere to any request for site recording of remains and artefacts through a written programme to be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority (in consultation with Historic England).  Reason: To ensure archaeological preservation in accordance with Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the commencement of the development (including demolition works) the developer shall submit written evidence to the local planning authority of a Bat Mitigation Class Licence (BMCL) issued by Natural England  for any disturbance, damage or destruction to any Bats habitat(s), including roosts, on the site.  The BCML must make provision for:Installation of one receptor bat box prior to demolition and construction works; Two integrated bat boxes into the new dwellings; andEcologist supervision during the removal of the shutter and potential bat exclusion.Any external lighting for the development must be implemented (and thereafter retained) to adhere to the Bat Conservation Trust/Institute of Lighting Professionals 'Bats and Artificial Lighting At Night' guidance (specifically GN 08/23). Guidance Note BN08/23 is mandatory to protect these commuting and foraging routes.Reason: To ensure that species and habitats are  protected in accordance with Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS3 and DM6 of the Core Strategy (2012).

If, during the course of development (including demolition works), any evidence of great crested newts (GCN) in the grounds is found which has not been previously identified, work shall be suspended and a GCN survey (following best practice) for the on-site pond shall be submitted to the local planning authority for its written approval before works re-commence. The survey should follow three methods (preferably torch survey, bottle-trapping and egg search) per visit, with 4 visits in suitable weather conditions between mid-March to mid-June, with at least two of these visits during mid-April to mid-May. This is required to determine presence/absence and discharge the legal risk associated with this European Protected Species.In the event that the survey identifies the pond (or its environs on site) as a breeding, resting or sheltering place for GCNs, then the developer shall submit written evidence to the local planning authority prior to the re-commencement of development (including demolition works) of a GCN Mitigation Licence issued by Natural England  for any disturbance, damage or destruction to any active GCN habitat(s) on the site.Reason: To ensure that species and habitats are  protected in accordance with Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS3 and DM6 of the Core Strategy (2012).

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/." Reason: To ensure the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policies D3, SI1 and T7 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The site and building works required to implement the development shall be only carried out between the hours of: 08.00 and 18.00 Mondays to Fridays and between 08.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays and not at all on Bank Holidays and Sundays.Reason: To ensure the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policies D3, SI1 and T7 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

a) No development (excluding demolition works) shall take place until a scheme of proposed noise mitigation measures against externally generated traffic/mixed use noise has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.b) The mitigation measures as approved under this condition shall be implemented in their entirety prior the first occupation of the development and retained as such thereafter.Reason: To ensure the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

a) No development other than demolition works shall commence on site in connection with the development hereby approved until a report has been carried out by a competent acoustic consultant that assesses the likely noise impacts of the ventilation/extraction plant, and mitigation measures for the development to reduce these noise impacts to acceptable levels and has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.The report shall include all calculations and baseline data and be set out so that the local planning authority can fully audit the report and critically analyse the content and recommendations.b) The measures approved under this condition shall be implemented in their entirety prior to the commencement of the use/first occupation of the development and retained as such thereafter.Reason: To ensure the amenity of future and neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The rating level of the noise from the plant hereby permitted shall be at least 5dBA lower than the existing background noise level at any given time of operation. The noise levels shall be measured or predicted 1m externally to any window at the nearest residential facade. Measurements and assessment shall be made according to British Standard 4142:2014.Reason: To ensure the amenity of future and neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

a) Prior to the commencement of the development (other than demolition works), a scheme of proposed air pollution mitigation measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.b) The approved mitigation scheme shall be implemented in its entirety in accordance with details approved under this condition before any of the development is first occupied or the use commences and retained as such thereafter.Reason: To ensure the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with policies D3, SI1 and T7 of the London Plan (2021) and policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

(a) Prior to first occupation of the dwellinghouses hereby approved, a detailed landscaping scheme including details of trees (including their maturity)/plants to be planted, wildflowers (the species, size and age), shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submitted landscaping scheme shall make provision for the planting of native trees/plant species and shall not include ivy (hedera) planting. (b) The scheme approved under part (a) shall be implemented within the first planting season following completion of the development and any tree planting and landscaping shall thereafter be maintained for five years to the satisfaction of the local planning authority. Any tree planting or landscaping which dies within 5 years of planting shall be replaced with a tree or vegetation of a similar size and species. Reason: In the interests of visual amenity and also that the local planning authority shall be satisfied as to the details of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition works), details of hard landscaping of any part of the site not occupied by buildings (including details of the permeability of hard surfaces) shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interests of visual amenity and also that the local planning authority shall be satisfied as to the details of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition works), full details of the proposed boundary treatments including any gates, walls or fences shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Once approved the boundary treatments shall be implemented in full prior to first occupation of the dwellinghouses and shall be thereafter permanently retained.Reason: To ensure the boundary treatment is of adequate design in the interest of visual and residential amenity and also that the local planning authority shall be satisfied as to the details of the development in accordance with Policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the measures set out in the Canopy Consulting Arboricultural Impact Assessment and Method Statement  (Rev. D)  dated June 2026 and the associated Tree Protection Plan dwg No. 25-1924-TPP-C dated June 2026.  The approved measures shall be implemented prior to commencement of any work (including demolition works) on site and maintained to the reasonable satisfaction of the local planning authority until the completion of the development. Reason: To safeguard trees worthy of retention and in the interests of the character and appearance of the area, in accordance with Policy G7 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Each off-street car parking space shown on the approved plans shall be provided with a hardbound, adequately-drained, dust-free surface prior to beneficial occupation of the development to which this permission relates and shall be permanently retained and kept free from obstruction thereafter. It shall not be used for any purposes other than the parking of vehicles for the occupiers of and visitors to the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of adequate off-street parking in the interests of the safety and operation of the highway network, in accordance with Policy T4 of the London Plan (2012) and Policies CS7 and DM9 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved a minimum 1 active  Electric Vehicle Charging Point (EVCP) shall be provided on site and provision shall be made for 3 passive EVCPs. The EVCP provision shall be fully implemented and made available for use prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved and shall thereafter be retained for use at all times. Reason: To promote sustainable travel choice in accordance with Policy T6.1 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the first occupation of the development evidence (e.g. photographs and installation contract) demonstrating that the sustainable drainage features for the development has been completed in accordance with the provisions specified in the Jomas Drainage and SUDS Strategy dated July 2025  shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing. Once implemented the features shall be implemented in full prior to first occupation of the dwellinghouses and shall be thereafter permanently retained.Reason: To ensure the development is made safe without increasing flood risk elsewhere in accordance with Policy SI13 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy DM4 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Any external lighting installed at the site shall be angled so as to prevent any spillage or glare beyond the site's boundaries and must be implemented (and thereafter retained) to adhere to the Bat Conservation Trust/Institute of Lighting Professionals 'Bats and Artificial Lighting At Night' guidance (specifically GN 08/23). Guidance Note BN08/23 is mandatory to protect these commuting and foraging routes. Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy DM10 of the Core Strategy (2012).

Prior to the commencement of above ground works (excluding demolition), of the development hereby approved, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Biodiversity Gain Plan must include:a)  information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat;b)  the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;c)  the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;d)  any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development;e)  any biodiversity credits purchased for the development; andf)  any such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.Reason: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain on site in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Notice in writing shall be given to the Council when the:a)  Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan has been implemented; andb)  Habitat creation and enhancement works as set out in the Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan have been completed.The created and/or enhanced habitat specified in the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan for the agreed time period.Reason: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain on site in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the occupation of development hereby approved, a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan, prepared in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan and including the below matters, shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan must include: a)  a non-technical summary;b)  the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan;c)  the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;d)  the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development;e)  the monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority.Reason: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain on site in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

No occupation shall take place until:a)  the habitat creation and enhancement works set out in the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan have been completed; andb)  a completion report, evidencing the completed habitat enhancements, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The created and/or enhanced habitat specified in the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan.Reason: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain on site in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Monitoring reports shall be submitted to the local planning authority in writing in accordance with the methodology and frequency specified in the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan. Reason: To ensure the development delivers a biodiversity net gain on site in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
